# 1. Introduction In this reference for the API 2.0, we explain the possible REST API requests for managing and configuring the Myra Suite via the Myra API. The APIv2 and documentation are continuously being developed. New functions and changes to the API will be announced at regular intervals.
## 1.1 What is API 2.0? The web API of Myra is based on REST using the HTTP requests for the messages. We are supporting programmatic access to almost every operation you can do on our web interface. You can manage your cache settings accordingly to your deployment cycle or change your DNS settings, to name a few.
## 1.2 Target group This reference is aimed at IT specialists and developers with the necessary knowledge of how to use REST APIs and who want to use it to integrate the Myra solution into their infrastructure or to automate it.
## 1.3 Documents to handle The reference guide for the Myra APIV2.0 is part of the documentation for the Myra Suite. You can access all documents via the dashboard of the Myra App. Depending on the interface design, you have two options for accessing the Myra App documentation. To access the Myra App documentation via the classic interface: 1. Open the Myra App website. 2. Log in. 3. Click the **Myra Application** button. 4. In the menu bar, click on **Account**. 5. Click on **Documents** in the list. To access the Myra App documentation via the new interface: 1. Open the Myra App website. 2. Log in. 3. Click the **Myra Application** button. 4. Click on the tab **Help & support**. 5. Under **Information**, click **Documentation**.
--- --- # 2. First Steps In this chapter we described all needed information to get ready to start with the API calls. This includes information about the access and examples for the creation of a first request. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The steps that a user must perform in the Myra App's web interface relate to the new user interface. >> ---
## 2.1 Use signature for authentication
### 2.1.1 Getting the API key and API secret To get the personal API key perform the following steps: 1. Open the Myra App. 2. Login in with your user account. 3. Click on your profile symbol in the upper right corner. 4. Click on **Personal Account** button. - The view **Personal account** opens. 5. Click on the **API access** tab. 6. Click under the **API access** tab on the **API Keys** tab. 7. Click under the **API Keys** tab on the **Create new API key** button. - The **Create new API key** dialog opens. 8. Add under the field **Name** an unique name for the API key. 9. Click on the **Next** button. - An overview with the **Name**, **Token (API key)** and the **Secret** appears. >> --- >> **Note:** >> Please save the secret key in a safe place. After clicking on the **I saved the secret** button, the secret key can no longer be viewed. >> --- 10. Click on **I saved the secret** button to close the dialog. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The API key has the same permissions as the user. >> ---
---
### 2.1.2 Getting access to the API >> --- >> **Note:** >> The following example are in Bash Script for Linux. For other operating system please modify the quotations related to the specific needs. >> ---
#### 2.2.2.1 Shell scripting for GET and DELETE requests To send a GET or DELETE requests to the API you need to provide a Bash script without a ``BODY`` and the following structure: === Start === ``` #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail ``` === Credentials === ``` API_KEY="" API_SECRET="" ``` === Request target === ``` HOST="https://apiv2.myracloud.com" URI="" METHOD="" CONTENT_TYPE="application/json" BODY="" ``` === Date (with colon in timezone, like moment().format()) === ``` DATE="$(date +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%:z")" ``` === MD5 of body === ``` if [[ -z "$BODY" ]]; then BODY_MD5="d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e" else BODY_MD5="$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | md5sum | awk '{print $1}')" fi ``` === Signing string === ``` SIGNING_STRING="${BODY_MD5}#${METHOD}#${URI}#${CONTENT_TYPE}#${DATE}" ``` === Keys (CryptoJS semantics: hex string keys) === ``` DATE_KEY_HEX="$(printf '%s' "$DATE" \ | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"MYRA${API_SECRET}" -hex \ | awk '{print $2}')" SIGNING_KEY_HEX="$(printf '%s' "myra-api-request" \ | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"$DATE_KEY_HEX" -hex \ | awk '{print $2}')" ``` === Signature === ``` SIGNATURE="$(printf '%s' "$SIGNING_STRING" \ | openssl dgst -sha512 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"$SIGNING_KEY_HEX" -binary \ | base64 | tr -d '\n')" ``` === Debug (safe) === ``` echo "DATE: $DATE" echo "SIGNING_STRING: $SIGNING_STRING" echo "Authorization: MYRA ${API_KEY}:${SIGNATURE}" ``` === Request === ``` curl -vvv "${HOST}${URI}" \ -H "Content-Type: ${CONTENT_TYPE}" \ -H "Date: ${DATE}" \ -H "Authorization: MYRA ${API_KEY}:${SIGNATURE}" \ -X "$METHOD" ```
#### 2.1.2.2 Shell scripting for POST and PUT requests To send a POST or PUT requests to the API you need to provide the following Bash script with a ``BODY`` and the needed object information for the end point inside of it. === Start === ``` #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail ``` === Credentials === ``` API_KEY="" API_SECRET="" ``` === Request target === ``` HOST="https://apiv2.myracloud.com" URI="" METHOD="" CONTENT_TYPE="application/json" ``` === JSON body with the needed VO object with relevant attributes for the request. === ``` BODY='{ "":"", "":"", "":"" },' ``` === Date (with colon in timezone, like moment().format()) === ``` DATE="$(date +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%:z")" ``` === MD5(body) === ``` BODY_MD5="$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | md5sum | awk '{print $1}')" ``` === Signing string === ``` SIGNING_STRING="${BODY_MD5}#${METHOD}#${URI}#${CONTENT_TYPE}#${DATE}" ``` === HMAC (CryptoJS semantics: hex-string keys) === ``` DATE_KEY_HEX="$(printf '%s' "$DATE" \ | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"MYRA${API_SECRET}" -hex \ | awk '{print $2}')" SIGNING_KEY_HEX="$(printf '%s' "myra-api-request" \ | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"$DATE_KEY_HEX" -hex \ | awk '{print $2}')" SIGNATURE="$(printf '%s' "$SIGNING_STRING" \ | openssl dgst -sha512 -mac HMAC -macopt key:"$SIGNING_KEY_HEX" -binary \ | base64 | tr -d '\n')" ``` === Debug === ``` echo "DATE: $DATE" echo "SIGNING_STRING: $SIGNING_STRING" echo "Authorization: MYRA ${API_KEY}:${SIGNATURE}" ``` === Request (verbose) === ``` curl -vvv "${HOST}${URI}" \ -H "Content-Type: ${CONTENT_TYPE}" \ -H "Date: ${DATE}" \ -H "Authorization: MYRA ${API_KEY}:${SIGNATURE}" \ --data-binary "$BODY" ```
---
## 2.2 Use token for authentication ### 2.2.1 Getting the API token To get the personal API token perform the following steps: 1. Open the Myra App. 2. Login in with your user account. 3. Click on your profile symbol in the upper right corner. 4. Click on **Personal Account** button. - The view **Personal account** opens. 5. Click on the **API access** tab. 6. Click under the **API access** tab on the **API Tokens** tab. 7. Click under the **API Tokens** tab on the **Create new API token** button. - The **Create new API token** dialog opens. 8. Add under the field **Name** an unique name for the API token. 9. Add under the field **Expiry date** an expiry date for the token. 10. Click on the **Create token** button. - An overview with the **Name** and **Token** appears. >> --- >> **Note:** >> Please save the token in a safe place. After clicking on the **I saved the token** button, the token can no longer be viewed. >> --- 11. Click on **I saved the token** button to close the dialog. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The API token has the same permissions as the user. >> --- ### 2.2.2 Getting access to the API with token To send a requests to the API you need to do the following: 1. Add the method to the request. 2. Add the the address of the API together with the URI, e.g. ``https://apiv2.myracloud.com/domains/1234``. 3. Add the token as Bearer Token as authorization to the header, e.g. ``-H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN"`` 4. For PUT and POST requests add a body in JSON to the request with the needed information. The request should be look like the following: For example: ``` curl -X GET "https://``apiv2.``myracloud.com/domains/1234" -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" ``` ---
## 2.3 Used API methods The Myra API used the following methods: | Name | Description | | -------- | ------- | | GET | The GET method allows you to request a specific object or a list of objects of settings and entries in the Myra App. | | POST | The POST method allows you to add new settings or entries for specific functions in the Myra App. | | PUT | The PUT method allows you to change specific information of existing settings or entries in the Myra App. Only the Attributes ``id``, ``modified`` and the attributes for changing a specific option need to be defined in the body. One exception are the subdomain setting where the PUT method works as a normal PUT and all possible values need to be defined. Otherwise existing settings will be overwritten with default settings | | DELETE | The DELETE method allows you to delete entire entries of an option in the Myra App. |
---
## 2.4 Possible responses All API calls return an HTTP response code of 200 with one of two different object types or, in an error case, an appropriate HTTP error code.
An object ``QueryVO`` is returned when receiving a list of objects from a GET request. | Attribute | Description | | -------- | ------- | | error | Shows if the requests had an error. | | list | A list of matches for the given page. | | page | The number of the current page. | | count | The number of hits. | | pageSize | The number of maximum matches per page. |
An object ``ResultVO`` is returned for successful requests for POST, PUT and DELETE. | Attribute | Description | | -------- | ------- | | error | Shows if the requests had an error. | | violationList | A list of objects ``ViolationVO`` to show validation errors`.| | targetObject | A list of all processed objects. |
| Attribute | Description | | -------- | ------- | | path | The name of the attribute which was not correctly validated. | | message | An error message which describes the problem.|
In addition to the object responses to a request, the following HTTP codes may occur. | Status code | Description | Response | | -------- | ------- | ------- | | 200 OK | The request has succeeded. | QueryVO | | 201 Created | The request has succeeded and a new object has been created as a result. | ResultVO | | 202 Accepted | The request has succeeded but not been completed yet. | ResultVO | | 400 Bad Request | The request has not succeeded. The request was incorrect or information is missing. | ViolationVO | | 401 Unauthorized | The request has not succeeded because the user authentication was incorrect. | ViolationVO | | 403 Forbidden | The request has not succeeded because the user does not have the right permissions. | ViolationVO |
---

# 3. Initial configuration The following sections explain how you can perform important initial configurations of the Myra App using the API.
## 3.1 Set up your first domain >> --- >> **Note:** >> If you store an SSL/TLS certificate for an encrypted connection between the user to Myra and between Myra to your origin server, the SSL/TLS certificate must be uploaded before the traffic is redirected to Myra. Otherwise, your website will be temporarily unavailable. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If you upload an SSL/TLS certificate to the Myra App, you must also upload a certificate to your origin server. Otherwise, encrypted communication between Myra and your origin server will not work. >> ---
Before your websites are protected by Myra and you can use all the features and settings of the Myra app, you must register your domains and a valid SSL/TLS certificate in the Myra App.
To set up your first domain, proceed as follows: 1. Set up the API. 2. Add a new domain at least with a domain name, see end point "POST ``/domains``". >> --- >> **Note:** >> At least the domain name must be set in the body with the attribute ``name``. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If the attribute ``autoDns`` is set to ``true``, Myra searches for existing DNS records based on a list of common subdomain names and saves the results in the DNS settings. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If you enabled the automatic search for DNS entries when creating the new domain, the first DNS entries will already be available. >> In this case, use "GET ``/domain/{domainId}/dns-records``" to get a list of all existing DNS records. >> If you need to change the existing entries use "PUT ``/domain/{domainId}/dns-records/{id}``". 3. Create one or more DNS records, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/dns-records``". >> --- >> **Note:** >> Please set also as default the attribute ``active`` to ``true`` or do it later. >> The value of ``active`` needs to be ``true`` to activate the protection by Myra for your domains and subdodmains. >> --- 4. Add a new SSL/TLS certificate for for the new DNS records, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/certificates``". 5. Switch the traffic of you domains and subdomains to Myra. You have two options: - Set Myra as the authoritative name server with your provider In this case, all requests to your origin server will be routed directly through Myra's servers. The advantage of moving your name server to Myra is that your DNS will be protected by Myra. In order for Myra to become your new name server, you must set Myra's name servers as DNS entries with your provider. - .AT-domains: a.myradns.at, b.myradns.at, c.myradns.at - .CH-domains: a.myradns.ch, b.myradns.ch, c.myradns.ch - .CO.UK-domains: a.myradns.co.uk, b.myradns.co.uk, c.myradns.co.uk - .DE-domains: a.myradns.de, b.myradns.de, c.myradns.de - .FR-domains: a.myradns.fr, b.myradns.fr, c.myradns.fr - .NL-domains: a.myradns.nl, b.myradns.nl, c.myradns.nl - All other domains: a.myradns.net, b.myradns.net, c.myradns.net - Use your own name server Enter the alternative CNAME entries of your DNS entries stored in the Myra App in your provider's name server. You can find the alternative CNAME entries for your domains and subdomains by using "GET ``/domain/{domainId}/dns-records``" under the attribute ``alternativeCname``.
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The configurations are updated automatically and may take at least 7 minutes. For major changes, Myra recommends disabling the automatic update to avoid invalid configurations. >> ---

## 3.2 Set up CDN Before CDN can be used, it must be activated into the subdomain settings. To activate the CDN functionality you need to change the subdomain settings for your domain or subdomain, where you want to use CDN and set the attribute ``cache_enabled`` to ``true``, see end point "POST "``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/settings``".
### Life cycle of cache objects The life cycle of a cache object at Myra depends on several factors. Before a request is sent to the Origin, it goes through the following steps: - **Evaluation of cache rules with inclusion of exceptions**: An object is cached if caching is enabled in the backend, one of the configured caching rules takes effect, and the Origin returns a cacheable response. - **Exclusion of cachability based on the no-cache rules**: The resource will not be cached if the following conditions are present in the response from the Origin: - Cache-Control: (no-store|no-cache|private) - Cache-Control: max-age=0 - **Defining cachability based on the MIME type**: Cachable MIME types include the following: - image/* - text/(html|css|javascript|x-javascript|js) - application/(javascript|x-javascript|json) - .woff - .woff2 - **Defining cachability based on the HTTP status code**: The following HTTP status codes are cachable: - 200 OK - 206 Partial Content - 301 Moved Permanently - 304 Not Modified - 404 Not Found - **Normalization of the object to be cached and setting the TTL**: Cachable objects are cleared of additional headers. ### Create a new cache element for CDN To create an entry to cache an object for CDN you need to define a domain or subdomain where you want to cache the object and add one or more entry to the cache settings of this domain or subdomain, see end point POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``". - The following information need to be added to the body of the request: - ``path`` - ``ttl`` - ``noFoundttl`` - ``type`` - ``enforce`` - ``sort`` ### Configuration of caching TTLs The cache TTL can be set either via Myra or via the Origin - Cache-TTL like origin server: set the attribute ``ttl`` to ``0``. This causes the cache TTL to be taken over by the Origin unless it is excluded by a no-cache rule. - Cache TTL: selected time: The cache TTL set in the backend is used as the lifetime for Myra's cache and as "CacheControl: max-age" towards the browser only as long as none of the no-cache rules apply. To set a time in seconds, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``". - Enforce cache TTL: Forcing the cache TTL allows you to set the cache TTL in the backend regardless of the response returned by the Origin. Forcing the cache TTL is not applied in case of a no-cache rule. To enforce the ttl set the attribute ``enforce`` to ``true``. - Ignore no-cache header: The backend option "Ignore no-cache header" causes the no-cache header cache control (private|no-store|no-cache) to be ignored and therefore the response can be cached by Myra. To activate the "Ignore no-cache header", you need to change the attribute ``enforce_cache_ttl`` to ``true`` in the subdomain settings of the related domain or subdomain, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``". - Stale objects: Stale objects allow the delivery of cached objects after the cache TTL has expired, despite connection problems with the Origin. To activate the stale objects option, you need to change the attribute ``proxy_cache_stale`` to `one or more of the following options in the subdomain settings of the related domain or subdomain: - error, timeout -> An generic error or timeout occurred while connecting to the origin server, sending the request or reading the response. - invalid_header -> Invalid or empty response from the origin server. - http_500, http_502, http_503, http_504 -> Origin server responded with the matching response code. - off -> Completely disables the next_upstream behavior. - updating -> Allows sending a stale cached response while it is being updated to reduce connections to the origin servers. See end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``". >> --- >>**Note** >>Objects that are not in the cache at the time of the request cannot be delivered and will be answered with a gateway timeout (HTTP 504) or the error page configured in the backend. You can verify whether a resource was delivered by Myra as a stale object by checking the X-CDN header with the value "X-CDN: 2". >> --- - Cache version check: The backend configurable option "Revalidate expired cache objects" allows saving bandwidth. If cache version checking is enabled, the Origin is queried for a newer version of the cached object with "If-Modified-Since" and "If-None-Match" after the cache TTL expires. In the case of a constant version, the cached object is repeatedly held in the cache for the period of the cache TTL and delivered. To activate the "Revalidate expired cache objects", you need to change the attribute ``cache_revalidate`` to ``true`` in the subdomain settings of the related domain or subdomain, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``". ### Evaluation order of caching rules The caching rules are processed in the backend based on the order you can specify. As soon as a rule applies, it is then used for caching with Myra and subsequent caching rules are not considered further. To set up the order of the cache entries add to the attribute ``sort`` a number for the sorting, see end point "POST ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings``" or endpoint "``PUT ``/domain/{domainId}/{vHostName}/cache-settings/{id}``". ### Is a resource cached with Myra? You can determine whether a resource is cached with Myra or not by looking at the X-CDN header in the response header. If "X-CDN: 1" is present, the resource is delivered from Myra's cache. If the X-CDN is missing, the resource is not cached. You can inspect the response header with the developer tools of common web browsers or on the command line with wget or curl. You can differentiate the following about the X-CDN header: - X-CDN header missing: the resource has not been delivered from Myra's cache. - X-CDN: 1: the resource has been delivered from Myra's cache. - X-CDN: 2: the resource has been delivered as a stale object from Myra's cache.

get.summary: Lists all contact persons
get.description:
### Description The List-Contacts request allows the user to request a list of all contact persons of the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: none Objects: none
### Request To request a list of all contact persons, no additional information needs to be added to the path of the request. As a result, the user gets one or more objects ``OrganizationContactVO`` with the requested information. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``userId`` | | The id of the user related to the entry, if the contact person is a Myra App user. | | ``integer`` | | | | ``name`` | | The name of the contact person. | |``string``| |Name | | ``email`` | | The email address of the contact person. | | ``string`` | | Email Address | | ``phone`` | | The phone number of the contact person. | |``integer``| | Phone Number | | ``receiveSSLReminders`` | | Shows, if the contact person gets notifications about expiring certificates. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``receiveTrafficAlerts`` | | Shows, if the contact person gets traffic alert notifications. Not available to partner customer organizations. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``technicalPriority`` | | The priority of the contact person for technical issues. | | ``integer`` | | TECHNICAL CONTACT PRIORITY | | ``escalationPriority`` | | The priority of the contact person for escalations. | | ``integer`` | | ESCALATION CONTACT PRIORITY | | ``id`` | | The ID of the entry. | | ``integer``| | | | ``modified`` | | The last modification date in ISO 8601 format. | |``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``created`` | | The creation date in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)``| | |

400.description: The request has not succeeded. The request was incorrect or information is missing.

403.description: The request has not succeeded because the user does not have the right permissions.

401.description: The request has not succeeded because the user authentication was incorrect.

post.summary: Adds a contact person
post.description:
### Description The Add-Contact request allows the user to add a new contact person to the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: none Objects: ''OrganizationContactVO''
### Request To add a contact person to the organisation, no additional information needs to be added to the path of the request. For a detailed specification of which information is required to add a contact person, one or more objects ``OrganizationContactVO`` with the following attributes need to be defined in the body. You have the following two ways to add a contact person: #### Myra App user as contact person | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``userId`` | |The id of the user related to the entry, if the contact person is a Myra App user. | | ``integer`` | | |
The following attributes are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``receiveSSLReminders`` | | Defines, if the contact person gets notifications about expiring certificates. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``receiveTrafficAlerts`` | | Defines, if the contact person gets traffic alert notifications. Not available to partner customer organizations. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``technicalPriority`` | | Defines the priority of the contact person for technical issues. | | ``integer`` | | TECHNICAL CONTACT PRIORITY | | ``escalationPriority`` | | Defines the priority of the contact person for escalations. | | ``integer`` | | ESCALATION CONTACT PRIORITY |
#### None Myra App user as contact person | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``name`` | | The name of the contact person. | |``string``| |Name | | ``email`` | | The email address of the contact person. | | ``string`` | | Email Address |
The following attributes are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``phone`` | | The phone number of the contact person. | |``integer``| | Phone Number | | ``receiveSSLReminders`` | | Defines, if the contact person gets notifications about expiring certificates. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``receiveTrafficAlerts`` | | Defines, if the contact person gets traffic alert notifications. Not available to partner customer organizations. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``

### Description The Clear-Cache request allows the user to delete all cached files or specific cached files on all Myra nodes for all or selected domains and subdomains.

  • ``true``
  • ``false``
||Recursive| | ``resource`` | | The resources to be cleared from the cache.
**Note:** If the attribute is not set, the whole cache of the defined domain or subdomain will be cleared. ||``string``||Path| | ``bulk`` | | A list of resources to be cleared.
**Note:** If set, the resources attribute will be ignored. |||``array``||
The following options are available to clear the cache: - Deleting file-type from the cache: - ``fqdn``: The name of the Domain or Subdomain. - ``recursive``: ``true`` - ``resource``: The pattern to search for (for example: ``/*js``). - Delete the attribute ``bulk``. - Deleting all files of a domain or subdomain from the cache: - ``fqdn``: The name of the Domain or Subdomain. - ``recursive``: ``true`` - Delete the attribute ``resource``. - Delete the attribute ``bulk``. - Deleting all file from the cache for all domains and subdomains: - Delete the attribute ``Fqdn``. - ``recursive``: ``true`` - Delete the attribute ``resource``. - Delete the attribute ``bulk``. - Deleting cached files from all domains and subdomains from the cache: - Delete the attribute ``Fqdn``. - ``recursive``: ``true`` - ``resource``: The pattern to search for (for example: ``/*js``). - Delete the attribute ``bulk``. - Deleting a list of defined files from a domain or subdomain: - ``fqdn``: The name of the Domain or Subdomain. - ``recursive``: ``true`` or ``false`` - Delete the attribute ``resource``. - ``bulk``: Array of all cached file types (for example: ``"bulk": ["/*.css", "/*.txt"]``)

### Description The List-Custom-Configurations request allows the user to request the custom configurations that Myra has applied for a domain of the organisation. Entries exist on two levels: a domain-level entry describes the whole domain, a subdomain-level entry describes a single subdomain. Both levels are requested through this endpoint, the query parameter ``subDomainName`` selects which one.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` Objects: none
### Request To request the custom configurations of a domain, the **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` needs to be added to the path of the request. Without it, the request returns the domain-level entries only. | | ``string`` | | |
As a result, the user gets one or more objects ``CustomConfigurationVO`` with the requested information. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``type`` | | The kind of setting the entry describes. | |
  • ``feature``
  • ``header``
  • ``ssl_cipher``
| | Type | | ``name`` | | The name of the setting. | | ``string`` | | Name | | ``value`` | | The value of the setting. Free text, the accepted content depends on the type. | | ``string`` | | Value | | ``description`` | | An explanation of why the setting was applied. | | ``string`` | | Description | | ``id`` | | The ID of the entry. | | ``integer`` | | | | ``modified`` | | The last modification date in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``created`` | | The creation date in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)`` | | |
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The response is not paginated. It returns every entry of the requested scope. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The result is limited to the entries that Myra has released for the customer. Entries kept internal are not part of the response. >> ---

Empty for a domain verified on creation. | | ``array of strings`` | | ``recordValue`` | | The value of the consent TXT record. | | ``string`` | | ``conflictingNames`` | | For the blockers ``name_conflict`` and ``record_conflict``: the DNS record names of this domain that another organisation holds too. They have to be resolved before the next check can verify the domain. Empty otherwise. | | ``array of strings`` | | ``parentNsAtMyra`` | | Whether the parent zone is delegated to the Myra name servers, as seen by the last check. | | ``boolean`` | | ``lastCheckedAt`` | | When the TXT record was checked last. | | ``datetime`` | | ``lastCheckResult`` | | The result of the last check. | |

put.summary: Verifies a domain or revokes its verification (Myra agents only)
put.description:
### Description The Update-Domain-Verification request lets a Myra agent verify a domain pending verification after the ownership was checked out of band or revoke the verification of a domain. A revoked domain is taken off the platform like a deleted one while its configuration stays; only a Myra agent can verify it again.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` Objects: none This resource is available to Myra agents only, in the agent mode or while administrating the customer. Partner agents and customers receive a ``403``.
### Request To update the verification, the **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` needs to be added to the path of the request. The body is a JSON object with the following attributes: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``verified`` | | ``true`` verifies the domain, ``false`` revokes its verification. | | ``boolean`` | | ``note`` | | The reason, stored with the verification record. Mandatory, up to 255 characters. | | ``string`` | A missing or malformed attribute is answered with ``400`` and the code ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_VERIFIED_REQUIRED`` or ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_NOTE_REQUIRED`` on the attribute. As a result, the user gets the verification status of the domain (see Get-Domain-Verification). A change the state of the domain refuses is answered with ``409`` and a code: ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_ALREADY_VERIFIED``, ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_NOT_VERIFIED``, ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_DELETED``, ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_NO_ORGANIZATION``, ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_VERIFICATION_MISSING``, ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_NAME_CONFLICT`` or ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_RECORD_CONFLICT``. For the two conflicts the response lists the DNS record names of the domain that another organisation also holds in ``extraData.conflictingNames``; they have to be resolved first, there is no forced verification.

### Description The Check-Domain-Verification request asks the platform to look for the consent TXT record of a domain pending verification. The check runs asynchronously; the result appears in the verification status of the domain. The platform checks pending domains on its own as well, so this only shortens the wait.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` Objects: none
### Request To request a check, the **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` needs to be added to the path of the request. No body is required. The request is answered with ``202`` once the check is queued. Repeated requests are merged into one check. A check that cannot verify the domain is answered with ``409`` and a code: ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_ALREADY_VERIFIED`` (the domain is verified), ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_MANUAL_REVOKED`` (a Myra agent revoked the verification, only an agent can verify it again), ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_TOKEN_MISSING`` (the domain has no consent token, a Myra agent has to verify it), ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_CHECKED_RECENTLY`` (the last check ran less than a minute ago, request the check again later) or ``DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_VERIFICATION_MISSING``.

### Description The Change-IP-Filter request allows the user to change the settings of an IP filter entry of a subdomain of the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}``, **Subdomain name** ``{name}``, **IP-Filter-ID** ``{id}`` Objects: ''IpFilterVO''
### Request To change an IP filter entry of a domain, the **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}``, the **Subdomain name** ``{name}``, and the **IP-Filter-ID** ``{id}`` need to be added to the path of the request. For a detailed specification of which information is required to change an IP filter entry, the object ``IpFilterVO`` with the following attributes needs to be defined in the body: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``value`` | | The values in the format of an IP address or CIDR notation for the IP filter. | |
  • Single IP address
  • CIDR notation
  • Rage of IP addresses
| | IP | | ``type`` | | The type of the IP filter entry. | |
  • ``WHITELIST``
  • ``BLACKLIST``
  • ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``
| | Type | | ``id`` | | The ID of the entry. | | ``integer``| | | | ``modified`` | | The last modification date in ISO 8601 format. | |``string($date-time)`` | | |
The following attributes are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``SubdomainName`` | | The name of the subdomain for which the IP filter entry is used. | | ``string`` | | | | ``enabled`` | | The availability of the entry. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | Enabled |
The system returns the object ``IpFilterVO`` with the changed information.
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The body must include the attributes ``id`` and ``modified`` to identify the corresponding entry. >> --- >> **Note:** >> Make sure that the ID of the DNS record in the path of the request is the same as the value for the attribute ``id`` in the body. >> ---

get.summary: Exports the IP filter entries of a subdomain
get.description:
### Description The Export-IP-Filters request allows the user to request an export of all IP filter entries for a subdomain of the organisation as a CSV file.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}``; **Subdomain name** ``{vHostName}`` Objects: none
### Request To request the export of all IP filter entries of a subdomain, the **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` and the **Subdomain name** ``{vHostName}`` need to be added to the path of the request. The following optional query parameter is available to filter the exported entries: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``type`` | | Filters the exported entries by the type of the IP filter entry. If the parameter is not set, the entries of all types are exported. A value outside the listed values is ignored. | |
  • ``WHITELIST``
  • ``BLACKLIST``
  • ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``
  • ``ALLOWLIST``
  • ``BLOCKLIST``
  • ``ALLOWLIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``
| | Type |
As a result, the user gets a file in CSV format with the content type ``text/csv`` instead of a JSON object. The first line of the file contains the column names ``IP``, ``Expires on`` and ``Comments``. Each further line contains one IP filter entry with the following values separated by commas: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``IP`` | | The IP address or the IP address range of the IP filter entry in CIDR notation, for example ``192.0.2.0/24``. | | ``string`` | | IP | | ``Expires on`` | | The date and time until the IP filter entry is valid in ISO 8601 format. The value is empty if the entry has no expiry date. | | ``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``Comments`` | | The comment of the IP filter entry. The value is empty if the entry has no comment. | | ``string`` | | |
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The user must have at least READ permissions for the IP filters of the subdomain. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The file contains enabled and disabled IP filter entries. The attribute ``enabled`` and the type of an entry are not part of the file. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If the subdomain has no IP filter entries for the selected type, the file contains only the line with the column names. >> --- >> **Note:** >> For the query parameter ``type``, ``ALLOWLIST`` is an alias for ``WHITELIST``, ``BLOCKLIST`` is an alias for ``BLACKLIST`` and ``ALLOWLIST_REQUEST_LIMITER`` is an alias for ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``. >> ---

post.summary: Imports IP filter entries for a subdomain
post.description:
### Description The Import-IP-Filters request allows the user to add IP filter entries from a CSV file to the IP filters of a subdomain of the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}``; **Subdomain name** ``{vHostName}`` Objects: none
### Request To add IP filter entries from a CSV file, the **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` and the **Subdomain name** ``{vHostName}`` need to be added to the path of the request. In addition, the query parameter ``type`` must be added to the request. The following query parameter is required: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``type`` | | The type of the IP filter entries. All entries of the file are created with this type. A request without this parameter is rejected with HTTP status ``400``. | |
  • ``WHITELIST``
  • ``BLACKLIST``
  • ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``
  • ``ALLOWLIST``
  • ``BLOCKLIST``
  • ``ALLOWLIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``
| | Type |
The body of the request contains the IP filter entries as plain text in CSV format. Each line defines one IP filter entry. Empty lines are skipped. The values of a line are separated by commas and are defined in the following order: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``IP`` | | The IP address or the IP address range of the IP filter entry in CIDR notation, for example ``192.0.2.0/24``. This is the first value of the line. | | ``string`` | | IP |
The following values are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``Expires on`` | | The date and time until the IP filter entry is valid. This is the second value of the line. A value in another format is ignored and the entry is created without expiry date. | | ``string($date-time)`` in the format ``YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss`` or in ISO 8601 format with the time zone offset | | | | ``Comments`` | | The comment of the IP filter entry. This is the third value of the line. All further values of the line are added to the comment. | | ``string`` | | |
As a result, the user gets an object ``ResultVO`` with the outcome of the import. The HTTP status ``201`` is returned also if single lines could not be imported. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``error`` | | Shows if an entry of the file failed the validation. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``violationList`` | | A list with one object for each line that could not be imported. A line that is not a valid IP address or not in CIDR notation, such as a line with column names, is skipped and reported in this list. The attribute ``message`` contains the reason and the attribute ``propertyPath`` the affected attribute. | | ``array`` | | |
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The user must have at least CREATE permissions for the IP filters of the subdomain. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The file must not contain a line with column names. A line with column names, such as the first line of an exported file, is reported as invalid and skipped. >> --- >> **Note:** >> All imported entries are enabled. If an entry with the same IP address and the same type already exists for the subdomain, the system changes the existing entry instead of adding a new one. The expiry date and the comment of the existing entry are replaced by the values of the file. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If the same IP address range occurs more than once in the file, only its first line is used. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The type ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER`` does not support an expiry date. An entry with an expiry date for this type is rejected. >> --- >> **Note:** >> For the types ``WHITELIST`` and ``BLACKLIST``, only single IPv6 addresses are allowed (prefix length 128). >> --- >> **Note:** >> For the query parameter ``type``, ``ALLOWLIST`` is an alias for ``WHITELIST``, ``BLOCKLIST`` is an alias for ``BLACKLIST`` and ``ALLOWLIST_REQUEST_LIMITER`` is an alias for ``WHITELIST_REQUEST_LIMITER``. >> ---

### Description The List-Subdomains request allows the user to request a list of all subdomains of a domain of the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` Objects: none
### Request To request a list of all subdomains of a domain, the **Domain-ID** ``{domainId}`` needs to be added to the path of the request. The following optional query parameters are available to filter the results and to control the content and the pagination of the response: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``search`` | | Filters the results by a search term matched against the name of the subdomain. All subdomains that contain the search term are returned. | | ``string`` | | | | ``active`` | | Filters the results to subdomains that are protected by Myra. | |
  • ``true``
| | | | ``isActive`` | | Adds the attribute ``active`` to each subdomain entry. | |
  • ``true``
| | | | ``page`` | | The page number for paginated results. Minimum value: 1. | | ``integer`` | | | | ``pageSize`` | | The number of entries per page. Default: ``50``. Minimum value: 1. | | ``integer`` | | |
As a result, the user gets one or more objects with the requested information. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``id`` | | The ID of the subdomain. | | ``integer`` | | | | ``label`` | | The name of the subdomain without the trailing dot. | | ``string`` | | Subdomain | | ``value`` | | The name of the subdomain including the trailing dot. | | ``string`` | | | | ``name`` | | The name of the subdomain including the trailing dot. | | ``string`` | | | | ``access`` | | Shows if the user has access to the subdomain. The value is always ``true``. | |
  • ``true``
| | | | ``domainName`` | | The name of the domain to which the subdomain belongs. | | ``string`` | | | | ``domainId`` | | The ID of the domain to which the subdomain belongs. | | ``integer`` | | | | ``paused`` | | Shows if the subdomain is paused. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``isActive`` | | Shows if the subdomain is protected by Myra. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | Myra Protection | | ``monitored`` | | Shows if the monitoring of the subdomain is enabled. | |
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| | | | ``monitoredId`` | | The ID of the monitoring settings of the subdomain. post.summary: Adds a replication DNS zone
post.description:
### Description The Add-Replication-DNS-Zone request allows the user to add a replication DNS zone to the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: none Objects: ''ReplicationDnsZoneVO''
### Request To add a replication DNS zone, no additional information needs to be added to the path of the request. For a detailed specification of which information is required to add a replication DNS zone, the object ``ReplicationDnsZoneVO`` with the following attributes needs to be defined in the body: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``zoneName`` | | The name of the replication DNS zone as a fully qualified domain name without a trailing dot, for example ``example.com``. The name must contain at least two labels and the last label must consist of letters only. The maximum length is 253 characters. The name must not yet be used by another replication DNS zone and must not be the name of an existing domain. | | ``string`` | | | | ``masters`` | | The IP addresses of the primary name servers from which Myra replicates the zone. At least one IPv4 or IPv6 address is required. Duplicate addresses are removed. | | ``array[string]`` | | |
The following attributes are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``replicationMethod`` | | The zone transfer method that Myra uses to replicate the zone from the primary name servers. ``AXFR`` transfers the complete zone. ``IXFR`` transfers only the changes since the last transfer. ``IXFR_UDP`` transfers only the changes since the last transfer and uses the UDP protocol. If the attribute is not set, the system uses ``IXFR``. | |
  • ``AXFR``
  • ``IXFR``
  • ``IXFR_UDP``
| | | | ``tsigKeyName`` | | The name of the TSIG key that secures the zone transfer. If the attribute is set, the attributes ``tsigKeyAlgorithm`` and ``tsigKey`` are required. | | ``string`` | | | | ``tsigKeyAlgorithm`` | | The algorithm of the TSIG key. The attribute is required if ``tsigKeyName`` is set. | |
  • ``hmac-md5``
  • ``hmac-sha1``
  • ``hmac-sha224``
  • ``hmac-sha256``
  • ``hmac-sha384``
  • ``hmac-sha512``
| | | | ``tsigKey`` | | The secret of the TSIG key. The attribute is required if ``tsigKeyName`` is set. The system never returns the secret. | | ``string`` | | | | ``overrideSoaRefresh`` | | The refresh interval in seconds that overrides the refresh value of the zone. The value must be greater than 0. The attribute can only be set by Myra and is ignored in customer requests. | | ``integer`` | | |
The system responds by returning the object ``ReplicationDnsZoneVO`` with the information about the new entry. The object contains the attributes described in the Get-Replication-DNS-Zone request.
>> --- >> **Note:** >> A replication DNS zone is a zone for which Myra acts as secondary name server. Myra replicates the zone from the primary name servers in ``masters`` by zone transfer (AXFR or IXFR). >> ---
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The organisation must have the feature ``DNSZones`` enabled and the user must have ``CREATE`` permissions for replication DNS zones. Otherwise the system denies the request. >> ---
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The system rejects the request if the zone name is already used by a replication DNS zone, also of another organisation, or if the zone name is the name of an existing domain. >> ---
>> --- >> **Note:** >> If the attribute ``tsigKeyName`` is set, the attributes ``tsigKeyAlgorithm`` and ``tsigKey`` must be set too. If the attribute ``tsigKeyName`` is not set, TSIG is not used for the zone. >> ---
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The body does not include the attributes ``id``, ``created`` and ``modified``. These values are set by the system after the entry is created. >> ---

  • ``429``
  • ``500``
  • ``502``
  • ``503``
  • ``504``
  • ``9999``

Only error codes set to ``true`` are affected. >> The supported error codes are ``400``, ``404``, ``405``, ``413``, ``429``, ``500``, ``502``, ``503``, ``504`` and ``9999`` (``9999`` represents blocked requests). ### Description The Lists-Waiting-Room-Settings allows the user to request a list of all settings for a waiting room of the organisation.

### Request To request a list of all setting for a waiting room, the **Waiting-Room-ID** ``{id}`` needs to be added to the path of the request. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``name`` | | The name of the waiting room. | |``string``| |Name| |``maxConcurrent``| |The maximum number of visitors allowed on the Origin server at the same time. As soon as the value is exceeded, each additional visitor is directed to the waiting room. | |``integer``| |Max Visitors| |``sessionTimeout``| |The duration in seconds for which an inactive session can access the Origin server. If the session is not accessed again during the time, access for the session is deactivated. | |``integer``| |Session Timeout (Min)| |``waitRefresh``| |The duration in seconds after which the waiting page is reloaded. If the session is not accessed again after the third reload, the session is removed from the queue. | |``integer``| |Waiting Page refresh (sec)| |``paths``| |a path within the apex domain or subdomain for which the waiting room is to be valid. The path needs to be defined as a regular expression. The default value in the PATH field is ".". ### Description The List-WAF-Rules request allows the user to request a list of all WAF rule of a subdomain in the organisation.
### Requirements Values of the request: **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` Objects: none
### Request To request a list of all WAF rules, the **Domain-ID** ``{id}`` need to be added to the path of the request. As a result, the user gets one or more objects ``WafRuleVO`` with the requested information. The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| |``ruleType``| |The category of the WAF rule. | |For domain WAF rules: ``Domain``| || |``name``| |The name of the WAF rule. | |``string``| |Rule name| |``description``| |An individual description for the WAF rule. | |``string``| |Notes| |``logIdentifier``| |The short name who is shown in the log to identify the WAF rule. | |``string``| |Log identifier| |``subDomainName``| |The level at which the rule should take effect. | |Add the name of a subdomain or for general WAF rules ``ALL-`` or ``ALL-``. | |Domain| |``direction``| |The phase of the WAF rule for handling incoming or outgoing requests. | |Possible values:
  • ``in`` -> Request
  • ``out`` -> Response
| |Phase| |``sync``| || || || |``actions``| |An array of all actions of a WAF rule. | |``WafActionVO``| |Actions| |``conditions``| |An array of all conditions of a WAF rule with the object. | | ``WafConditionVO``| |Conditions| |``sort``| |The ascending order for the entry. | |Possible values: ``0`` or upper| |Sort| |``enabled``| |The availability of the WAF rule. | |Default: ``true``

Possible values:
  • ``true``
  • ``false``
| |State| |``expireDate``| |The date as ISO 8601 until the WAF rule is valid. | |Default: ``NULL``| |Expiry Date| |``comment``| |An individual comment for the WAF rule. | |``string``| |Notes| |``template``| |Indicate whether the WAF rule is part of a template. | || || |``processNext``| |Defines if the conditions of a WAF rule continues after a condition is matched. | |Default: ``false``

| |Options -> Process next rule| |``copiedFrom``| |Defines if the WAF rule is a copy of another rule. | || || | ``id`` | | The ID of the entry. | | ``integer``| | | | ``modified`` | | The last modification date in ISO 8601 format. | |``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``created`` | | The creation date in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)``| | |

post.summary: Gets statistics for domains and subdomains by data source
post.description:
### Description The Statistic-Query request allows the user to request statistics for one or more data sources for the domains and subdomains of the organisation for a selected time period.
### Requirements Values of the request: none Objects: ''StatisticVO''
### Request To request statistics, no additional information needs to be added to the path of the request. For a detailed specification of which information is required to request statistics, the object ``StatisticVO`` with the following attribute needs to be defined in the body: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``query`` | | The definition of the statistics query. | | ``StatisticQueryVO`` | | |
The object ``query`` requires the following attributes: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``startDate`` | | The start of the time period in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``endDate`` | | The end of the time period in ISO 8601 format. | | ``string($date-time)`` | | | | ``dataSources`` | | The data sets to request. Each entry has a freely selectable name as key and an object with the attributes ``source`` and ``type`` as value. At least one entry must be defined. | | ``object`` | | |
The following attributes are optional: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``type`` | | Defines for which domains the statistics are calculated. The default value is ``fqdn``. | |
  • ``fqdn``
  • ``all``
  • ``own``
  • ``foreign``
| | | | ``fqdn`` | | A list with the names of the domains and subdomains for which the statistics are calculated. The attribute is required if the attribute ``type`` is ``fqdn`` and ignored for all other values. | | ``array[string]`` | | | | ``aggregationInterval`` | | The interval of the data points of data sets with the type ``histogram``. The default value is ``day``. | |
  • ``2m``
  • ``hour``
  • ``day``
  • ``week``
  • ``month``
  • ``year``
| | |
**Query type** ``type`` defines for which domains the statistics are calculated. The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| | ``fqdn`` | | The statistics are calculated for the domains and subdomains defined in the attribute ``fqdn``. The user must have at least READ permissions for each of them. | | ``all`` | | The statistics are calculated for all domains that the user can access. The attribute ``fqdn`` is ignored. | | ``own`` | | The statistics are calculated for all domains that the user can access, as for ``all``. The attribute ``fqdn`` is ignored. | | ``foreign`` | | The statistics are calculated for all domains that the user can access, as for ``all``. The attribute ``fqdn`` is ignored. |
**Fqdn** ``fqdn`` defines the domains and subdomains by name, for example ``example.com`` or ``www.example.com``. To include a domain with all its subdomains, the name must be defined with the prefix ``ALL:``, for example ``ALL:example.com``.
**Aggregation interval** ``aggregationInterval`` defines the data points of data sets with the type ``histogram``. The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| | ``2m`` | | The data points are shown every two minutes within the specified time period. | | ``hour`` | | The data points are shown every 60 minutes within the specified time period. | | ``day`` | | The data points are shown every 24 hours within the specified time period. | | ``week`` | | The data points are shown every 7 days within the specified time period. | | ``month`` | | The data points are shown every month within the specified time period. | | ``year`` | | The data points are shown every year within the specified time period. |
Each entry of the object ``dataSources`` requires the following attributes: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``source`` | | The data source from which the data set is calculated. | | ``string`` | | | | ``type`` | | The aggregation type that defines the format of the data set. | |
  • ``stats``
  • ``histogram``
  • ``top``
| | |
**Type** ``type`` of a data set defines the format of the data set. The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| | ``stats`` | | The data set contains the summarised values for the whole time period. | | ``histogram`` | | The data set contains one value for each data point of the time period. The attribute ``aggregationInterval`` defines the distance of the data points. | | ``top`` | | The data set contains a list of the most requested URLs with the number of requests. |
**Source** ``source`` of a data set defines which data is calculated. Unless stated otherwise, the following values are available for the types ``stats`` and ``histogram``: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| | ``requests`` | | The total number of requests. | | ``requests_total`` | | The total number of requests. The data source returns the same values as ``requests``. | | ``requests_ssl`` | | The number of requests over HTTPS. | | ``requests_nonssl`` | | The number of requests over HTTP. | | ``requests_cached`` | | The number of requests that were answered from the cache. | | ``requests_cached_ssl`` | | The number of cached requests over HTTPS. | | ``requests_cached_nonssl`` | | The number of cached requests over HTTP. | | ``requests_uncached`` | | The number of requests that were forwarded to the origin server. | | ``requests_uncached_ssl`` | | The number of uncached requests over HTTPS. | | ``requests_uncached_nonssl`` | | The number of uncached requests over HTTP. | | ``requests_blocked`` | | The number of blocked requests. | | ``requests_blocked_reason`` | | The number of blocked requests grouped by the reason for blocking. | | ``bytes`` | | The total amount of traffic in bytes. | | ``bytes_ssl`` | | The amount of traffic over HTTPS in bytes. | | ``bytes_nonssl`` | | The amount of traffic over HTTP in bytes. | | ``bytes_cached`` | | The amount of traffic answered from the cache in bytes. | | ``bytes_cached_ssl`` | | The amount of cached traffic over HTTPS in bytes. | | ``bytes_cached_nonssl`` | | The amount of cached traffic over HTTP in bytes. | | ``bytes_uncached`` | | The amount of traffic delivered from the origin server in bytes. | | ``bytes_uncached_ssl`` | | The amount of uncached traffic over HTTPS in bytes. | | ``bytes_uncached_nonssl`` | | The amount of uncached traffic over HTTP in bytes. | | ``response_codes`` | | The number of requests grouped by HTTP status code. | | ``country_codes`` | | The number of requests grouped by the country code of the client. | | ``requests_cache_hits`` | | The ratio of cached requests. | | ``requests_cache_hits_ssl`` | | The ratio of cached requests over HTTPS. | | ``bytes_cache_hits`` | | The ratio of cached traffic. | | ``bytes_cache_hits_ssl`` | | The ratio of cached traffic over HTTPS. | | ``requests_blocked_hits`` | | The ratio of blocked requests. | | ``upstream_performance`` | | The average response time of the origin server for uncached requests. | | ``requests_cache_hits_nonssl`` | | The ratio of cached requests over HTTP. Available only for the type ``histogram``. | | ``bytes_cache_hits_nonssl`` | | The ratio of cached traffic over HTTP. Available only for the type ``histogram``. | | ``url_hits`` | | The most requested URLs that were answered from the cache. Available only for the type ``top``. | | ``cache_misses`` | | The most requested URLs that were not answered from the cache. Available only for the type ``top``. |
As a result, the user gets an object ``StatisticVO`` with the requested information. The object ``query`` contains the values of the request. The object ``result`` contains one entry for each entry of ``dataSources``, named as the key of the entry. The object ``result`` provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``result`` | | The data sets of the request. The content of each data set depends on the attribute ``type`` of the related data source. | | ``object`` | | |
A data set of the type ``stats`` provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``min`` | | The minimum value of the time period. | | ``number`` | | | | ``max`` | | The maximum value of the time period. | | ``number`` | | | | ``sum`` | | The sum of the values of the time period. | | ``number`` | | | | ``avg`` | | The average value of the time period. | | ``number`` | | |
A data set of the type ``stats`` for the sources ``requests_cache_hits``, ``requests_cache_hits_ssl``, ``bytes_cache_hits``, ``bytes_cache_hits_ssl``, ``requests_blocked_hits`` and ``upstream_performance`` contains only the attribute ``avg``. For the sources ``response_codes``, ``country_codes`` and ``requests_blocked_reason``, the data set contains the listed values for each status code, country code or reason.
A data set of the type ``histogram`` contains one object for each data point. The name of the object is the timestamp of the data point. Each object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``value`` | | The value of the data point. If there is no data for the data point, the value is ``0``. | | ``number`` | | |
A data set of the type ``top`` contains one entry for each URL. The name of the entry is the URL and the value is the number of requests of the URL.
>> --- >> **Note:** >> The user must have at least READ permissions for the requested domains and subdomains. >> --- >> **Note:** >> The difference between ``startDate`` and ``endDate`` must not exceed 7952399 seconds (about 92 days). >> --- >> **Note:** >> A maximum of 150 domains and subdomains can be requested in one query. >> --- >> **Note:** >> If the attribute ``type`` is ``fqdn``, each name in ``fqdn`` must be an existing domain or subdomain. A name for which the user has no READ permissions causes an error. >> ---

**Interval** ``{interval}`` defines the data points used to calculate the data. The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| |``2m``||The data points are shown every two minutes within the specified time period.| |``hourly``||The data points are shown every 60 minutes within the specified time period.| |``daily``||The data points are shown every 24 hours within the specified time period.| |``weekly``||The data points are shown every 7 days within the specified time period.|
**Sum** ``{sum}`` defines if the data for all domains and subdomain should be accumulated into one chart. The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| |``0``||The data for each domain and subdomain will be shown separately.| |``1``||The data for each domain and subdomain will be shown as an accumulated total.|

The following values are available: | Value |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| |``0``||Empty data points are retained in the chart.| |``1``||Empty data points are removed from the chart.|

The object provides the following information: | Attribute |           | Description |           | Values |           | Name in Myra App | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | ``x`` | | The date and time for the data point. || ``integer`` as unix timestamp || | | ``y`` | | The value for the related data point. || ``integer``|| | | ``max`` | | The maximal value of the data point. ||``integer``||| | ``name`` | | The name of the chart as defined by the **Chart** ``{chartName}`` parameter. ||``integer``||| | ``sum`` | | Shows if the data is accumulated or not. ||``integer``||| | ``time`` | | Shows the the unix timestamp related to the max value. ||``date``|||

post.summary: Creates a managed certificate request
post.description:
### Description The Create-Managed-Certificate-Request request creates a new managed certificate request from a ``SslCertRequestVO``. The provider, the subject alternative names and the assignments define what is requested. Issuance is asynchronous: the request status moves to ``CREATED`` once the certificate has been issued. >> --- >> **Note:** >> A request requires the ``Myra-Certificate`` organisation feature. Sectigo and D-Trust additionally require provider credentials (see ``/ssl/providers``). >> ---
### Authentication The request is authenticated like every other call of this API, either with the API key signature or with an API token sent as ``Authorization: Bearer ``. See the introduction for how to create a key or a token.
### Request status The ``status`` attribute of the request reports the progress of the issuance: | Value |           | Meaning | |--------|--------|--------| | ``OPEN`` | | The request has been accepted and the certificate is being issued. | | ``WAITING_FOR_CNAME`` | | The issuance is waiting for the domain validation to succeed. | | ``CREATED`` | | The certificate has been issued and assigned to the subdomains of the request. | | ``FAILED`` | | The issuance did not succeed, see "Failure details" for the cause. The periodic renewal run tries the request again on its next pass, unless the request can never be issued as it is (for example 100 subject alternative names or more or a domain that no longer exists). |
### Failure details When an issuance or a renewal fails, the read-only attribute ``failureReason`` names the step that failed. If the certificate provider rejected or delayed the order, ``providerErrorCode`` names the cause and ``providerErrorDetail`` carries the message of the provider, if it sent one. ``customerActionable`` is ``true`` when the cause named by ``failureReason`` or ``providerErrorCode`` has to be resolved on the customer side. ``failureReason``, ``providerErrorCode`` and ``providerErrorDetail`` are omitted while there is nothing to report. They are cleared when the certificate is issued and whenever the request leaves the status ``FAILED``. For a failed renewal the ``status`` stays ``CREATED``, because the issued certificate keeps being served. | Value |           | Meaning | |--------|--------|--------| | ``PROVIDER_DOMAIN_NOT_AUTHORIZED`` | | A requested domain is not authorized in the provider account. Authorize or validate the domain there (Sectigo: Sectigo Certificate Manager, D-Trust: Certificate Service Manager). | | ``PROVIDER_APPROVAL_PENDING`` | | The order waits for an approval or for the organisation validation in the provider account. | | ``PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS_INVALID`` | | The provider does not accept the provider credentials of the request (EAB key ID or EAB HMAC key). Check them in the provider account and update them under ``/ssl/providers``. The EAB HMAC key has to be at least 256 bits long. | | ``PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_INVALID`` | | The endpoint of the provider credentials of the request does not lead to an ACME directory of the provider (the address was not found or the answer is not an ACME directory). Correct it under ``/ssl/providers``. | | ``PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED`` | | A rate limit of the provider has been reached. No action is required on the customer side. | | ``PROVIDER_CONFIGURATION_ERROR`` | | The provider setup on the Myra side is incomplete or wrong. No action is required on the customer side. | | ``PROVIDER_REJECTED`` | | The provider rejected the order for another reason. |
### Certificate chain By default the served certificate chain does not contain cross-signed copies of root certificates that current clients already trust. Set ``includeCrossSignedRoots`` to ``true`` to keep them, for clients with an outdated trust store (for example legacy Java or Android versions). The chain is then served as delivered by the certificate authority, including every cross-signed certificate it contains. For Sectigo these are ``Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46`` or ``E46`` cross-signed by USERTrust and the USERTrust certificate cross-signed by ``AAA Certificate Services``. Chain scanners can then report that the chain contains an anchor. A self-signed root certificate is never served. The attribute is accepted for every provider, today only Sectigo chains carry such cross-signed certificates. Default: ``false``.
### Rate limits Issuance is subject to the following limits. They are checked before the certificate is ordered and they apply to every provider, not only to Let's Encrypt: | Limit |           | Description | |--------|--------|--------| | 50 certificates per domain per week | | Counted per domain, so ``example.com`` covers ``www.example.com`` and ``api.example.com`` against the same limit. | | 300 orders per account per 3 hours | | Counted per certificate provider account. | | 5 certificates per week for the same set of subject alternative names | | Repeatedly re-issuing an unchanged request reaches this limit first. | | 99 subject alternative names per request | | The check rejects a set of 100 names or more, so 99 is the largest set that can be issued. | >> --- >> **Note:** >> A request that reaches one of these limits does **not** wait for the limit window to free up. For a first issuance the status becomes ``FAILED``. For the renewal of a certificate that has already been issued the request stays ``CREATED``, so a renewal never reports ``FAILED`` while the issued certificate keeps being served. In both cases the periodic renewal run retries on its next pass. >> ---
### End-to-end flow: Phase 1 (Let's Encrypt) 1. (Optional) Confirm the domains resolve as expected before requesting: ``` curl -X POST "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/requests/check-domains" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"domains": ["www.example.com"]}' ``` 2. Create the request. ``provider`` is ``LETS_ENCRYPT`` and ``algorithm`` is one of ``RSA2048``, ``ECDSA256`` or ``ECDSA384``: ``` curl -X POST "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/requests" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"provider": "LETS_ENCRYPT", "algorithm": "RSA2048", "subjectAlternativeNames": [{"name": "www.example.com"}], "assignments": [{"subDomainName": "www.example.com"}]}' ``` 3. Poll the request until ``status`` turns to ``CREATED``, which means the certificate has been issued and assigned to the subdomain: ``` curl -X GET "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/requests/{id}" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" ```
### End-to-end flow: Phase 2 (Sectigo and D-Trust) 1. Add the provider credentials once per organisation (requires a root group member or organisation admin context). ``provider`` is ``SECTIGO`` or ``DTRUST``; Sectigo also needs the product ``endpoint``. The response returns the new credential ``id``: ``` curl -X POST "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/providers" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"name": "Sectigo OV", "provider": "SECTIGO", "endpoint": "https://acme.sectigo.com/v2/OV", "eabKid": "MY_EAB_KID", "eabHmac": "MY_EAB_HMAC"}' ``` 2. Create the request referencing that credential through ``sslProviderCredentialsId``. Sectigo and D-Trust additionally accept the algorithms ``RSA4096`` and ``RSA8192``, which Let's Encrypt rejects: ``` curl -X POST "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/requests" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"provider": "SECTIGO", "algorithm": "RSA2048", "sslProviderCredentialsId": 42, "subjectAlternativeNames": [{"name": "www.example.com"}], "assignments": [{"subDomainName": "www.example.com"}]}' ``` 3. Poll the request until ``status`` turns to ``CREATED``. The certificates issued for a credential can be listed at any time: ``` curl -X GET "https://apiv2.myracloud.com/ssl/providers/{id}/certificates" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer MY_API_TOKEN" ```

### Description
Updates the managed certificate request identified by **Request-ID** ``{id}`` from a ``SslCertRequestVO``.
Requires the ``Myra-Certificate`` organisation feature.

>> ---
>> **Note:**
>> Adding a subject alternative name that no live certificate of the request already covers triggers the issuance of a new certificate. Removing a subject alternative name depends on the provider: for Let's Encrypt the issued certificate keeps covering the removed name until its next renewal, for Sectigo and D-Trust a narrowed certificate is re-issued. The key algorithm is immutable after creation.
>> ---

>> ---
>> **Note:**
>> An update replaces the whole request. An attribute that is omitted falls back to its default, so a request body without ``includeCrossSignedRoots`` switches the option off. Changing ``includeCrossSignedRoots`` does not issue a new certificate, the new value applies from the next issuance or renewal. See the Create-Managed-Certificate-Request description for what the option does.
>> ---

The attribute ``fqdn`` of each entry shows the subdomain the maintenance page is assigned to.
